stemMd:
A cube with edges of $6\ \text{cm}$ is shown in an isometric drawing seen from above: one set of edges is drawn vertically, the other two are drawn at $30^\circ$ above the horizontal, and **every edge is drawn at its full length of $6\ \text{cm}$**. On the sheet, the top face of the cube becomes a rhombus with one diagonal horizontal and the other vertical.

How long are these two diagonals on the drawing?
explanationMd:
**What to notice first.** Only lengths **parallel to the three axes** are drawn true in an isometric drawing. A diagonal of a face is not parallel to any axis, so its drawn length has to be worked out from the drawn edges; it will not be the real $6\sqrt{2}\ \text{cm}$.

**The step that settles it.** Put the corner of the top face nearest the viewer at the origin of the sheet. Its two top edges run to the right and to the left at $30^\circ$ above the horizontal, each $6\ \text{cm}$ long, so they end at

$$\left(6\cos 30^\circ,\ 6\sin 30^\circ\right) = \left(3\sqrt{3},\ 3\right) \quad\text{and}\quad \left(-3\sqrt{3},\ 3\right).$$

- The **horizontal** diagonal joins these two side corners: $3\sqrt{3} + 3\sqrt{3} = 6\sqrt{3} \approx 10.4\ \text{cm}$.
- The **vertical** diagonal joins the nearest corner to the farthest one, which is reached by adding both edge vectors: $(0,\ 3 + 3) = (0,\ 6)$. It is $6\ \text{cm}$.

**How to check it.** The rhombus has angles of $120^\circ$ at the nearest and farthest corners and $60^\circ$ at the side corners. Two of its sides and its vertical diagonal form a triangle with a $60^\circ$ angle between two equal sides, so that triangle is equilateral and the vertical diagonal equals a side, $6\ \text{cm}$. By Pythagoras on a quarter of the rhombus, $3^2 + (3\sqrt{3})^2 = 9 + 27 = 36 = 6^2$, which confirms the half-diagonals $3$ and $3\sqrt{3}$.

distractorRationale.a: Gives the real diagonal of the square face, $6\sqrt{2}$, for both. An isometric drawing keeps lengths true only along the three axes; the face becomes a rhombus whose diagonals are unequal.
distractorRationale.c: Has the right two lengths on the wrong diagonals. The side corners of the rhombus are $2 \times 3\sqrt{3}$ apart horizontally, while the nearest and farthest corners are only $3 + 3$ apart vertically, so the long diagonal is the horizontal one.
distractorRationale.d: Stops at the horizontal and vertical components of a single edge, $6\cos 30^\circ$ and $6\sin 30^\circ$. Each diagonal spans two edges, so both components must be doubled.
distractorRationale.e: Treats the horizontal diagonal as true length. It is true length only in the true isometric projection, where every axis is shortened to about 82% of its length; this drawing keeps edges at full length, which enlarges everything, that diagonal included, to $6\sqrt{3}$.

accessibilityText: A question on isometric drawing, with no figure needed. A cube with six-centimetre edges is drawn isometrically seen from above: one set of edges vertical, the other two at thirty degrees above the horizontal, and every edge drawn at its full six centimetres. The top face becomes a rhombus with one horizontal and one vertical diagonal, and the question asks for their lengths on the drawing. The choices are: both six root two, about eight point five centimetres; horizontal six root three, about ten point four centimetres, and vertical six centimetres; horizontal six centimetres and vertical six root three, about ten point four; horizontal three root three, about five point two, and vertical three centimetres; and horizontal six root two, about eight point five, and vertical six centimetres.

provenance.notes: Original item. A script placed the rhombus corners at (0, 0), (6 cos 30, 6 sin 30), (-6 cos 30, 6 sin 30) and (0, 6) and measured the diagonals as 10.3923 (6 root 3) and 6.0000 cm; the real face diagonal is 8.4853 (6 root 2) cm. The rhombus angle at the nearest corner is 120 degrees.

review.author: wave6-polito-til-a-drawing-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: The top-face edges are drawn as the vectors (6cos30, 6sin30) = (5.196, 3) and (-5.196, 3). Their sum (0, 6) is the vertical diagonal, 6 cm long. Their difference (10.39, 0) is the horizontal diagonal, 6 times root 3. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave7-tila-logic-drawing-run1) reached the same answer: Put the top face's near corner at the origin. Its two edges go to (+-6cos30, 6sin30) = (+-5.196, 3) and the far corner is at (0, 6). The horizontal diagonal is therefore 2 x 5.196 = 6 sqrt3 (about 10.4 cm) and the vertical diagonal is 6 cm. C swaps the two, and A and E use true-shape values.]

review.notes: Author's uniqueness check: the stem fixes the drawing convention (full-length edges, 30 degree axes), which determines both diagonals; every wrong choice differs in at least one of the two lengths. Awaiting a blind independent solve before publication. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
